newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - March 25.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - March 25.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:

* On Monday, the Dow Jones industrial average closed up 100.46 points at 6,905.25, recovering from a four-session string of losses that wiped 150 points off the blue-chip index. It was the biggest gain for the Dow since Feb. 12, when it rose more than 103 points.
Investors remained bullish even as they took for granted that the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at a policy-making meeting on Tuesday.

* Indonesia re-allows foreign palm oil investment, but they must be located in the eastern part of the country, news reports quoted Agriculture Minister Sjarifudin Baharsjah as saying on Monday. The government in early March announced it would not give any new investment permits for foreign investment in the palm oil sector.
* On Monday, the Jakarta Composite Index closed 6.50 points, or 0.99 percent lower, at 649.62 points
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,399.00/400.00 at 0150 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,401.00/02.00
* Property firm Suryamas on announcement on Tuesday it posted a sharp drop in its 1996 net profit.
* Semen Gresik, Daya Guna and Dharmala Sakti on announcements on Monday of their 1996 financial results.
* Automotive parts manufacturer Selamat Sampurna on market talk business tycoon Hutomo Mandala Putra was to link-up with the firm.
* Mulialand on reports the exchangable bonds issue of the firm's major shareholder PT Muliasentra Gunaswakarya was oversubscribed.
* Dharmala Intiland on reports it was likely to acquire another property firm Putra Surya Perkasa.
* Transportation firm Mitra Rajasa on market talk business tycoon Yopie Widjaja planned to acquire the firm. Widjadja had denied the rumour.
